name: Small LCD screen
description: A bare 7-inch display panel in a thin metal frame, its ribbon cable running to a small driver board.
notes: Lying screen up: a 165 mm by 100 mm panel 8 mm thick with a black bezel round a glossy screen, an aluminium back frame, a gold ribbon cable and a green driver board with a chip and a white plug. The mass follows the reference's 0.5 kg, heavy for so thin a panel. Using it in electronics crafting has no recipe yet.

name: Wet adobe brick
description: A freshly moulded brick of mud and chopped straw, still too soft to build with.
notes: A 250 mm by 125 mm by 75 mm block in clay-wet, its base slumped a little wider than its top, with straw-pale flecks on the top and sides. Drying it into a hard brick needs an item state or a timed transform that the drafts cannot express yet; the dry brick should get its own model in a lighter finish.

name: Mouldy soy and wheat cake
description: A pressed cake of soybeans and wheat grown over with pale mould, ready to brew into soy sauce.
notes: A 140 mm by 90 mm by 40 mm block in mushroom-pale under a fuzzy crust of fleece-pale lumps, with sage-green patches where the mould has started to sporulate. It is a brewing ingredient rather than something to eat, so it is filed as material. It is crafted, never found, so the economy entry is a placeholder at the lowest tier.

name: Spare wheel carrier
description: A swing-out steel arm that bolts to a rear bumper and carries a spare wheel on five studs.
notes: Lying flat: a charcoal-painted 50 mm square arm 700 mm long with a hinge plate and two knuckles at one end, a latch bar near the hinge, and a round wheel plate with a hub and five bright studs at the other, braced by two gussets. Combining it with a wheel into a vehicle part has no content field yet. The size is a placeholder for a thing too long for most packs.

name: Heavy coil spring
description: A heavy steel coil spring from a car's suspension.
notes: Built on the coil family: eight turns of 13 mm bar, 120 mm across and about 240 mm tall, in blackened steel. CHECK VOLUME (x4.5): the box counts the open middle of the coil; the reference's 0.75 L is close to the steel itself. The coil family draws stacked rings rather than a helix.

name: Spurge flowers
description: A handful of spurge stems topped with small yellow-green flowers, picked for tea.
notes: Five leaf-green stems about 160 mm long fanned from one end, each with a side leaf, a spray of sage bracts and a small yellow flower. No finish is the chartreuse of real spurge bracts, so cloth-sage stands in. Brewing it into a tea that eases breathing has no content field yet; the draft carries no medical effect.

name: Steel armour plate
description: A curved steel plate with the top corners cut, made to slide into the pocket of a vest.
notes: Lying strike face up: a 250 mm by 300 mm plate with shooter's cuts at the top corners, about 4 mm thick at the 2 mm grain, curved across, a dark grey spall coat (plastic-charcoal) on the face inside a bare steel-grey rim. The reference's 1 kg is light for steel of this size; the mass follows the reference. CHECK VOLUME is not raised; the box (x3.6) counts the curve. It is an insert, not a garment: it has no slot and is carried in a plate carrier's plate pocket. Its protection should count only while it sits in such a pocket, which has no content field yet, so `protects` records the plate's own figures for when it does. No damage type for bullets exists, so pierce stands in for it.

name: Straw doll
description: An old doll of bound straw, its lower half spread into a long skirt.
notes: 250 mm tall in straw-pale: a cone skirt with darker stalk ends at the hem, a narrow bodice, a round head, a twist of straw through the shoulders for arms, and red thread tied at the neck, waist and wrists. CHECK VOLUME (x9.1): the reference's 0.5 L is the straw; the box counts the air round a cone and outstretched arms.

name: Sunflower head
description: The cut head of a sunflower, its yellow petals ringing a broad disc of seeds.
notes: Lying face up: a 260 mm head with a domed brown seed disc 170 mm across and a dark centre, 24 yellow petals over 18 green bracts, on a green back with a stub of stalk. Picking its seeds out has no content field yet, so it carries no nutrition of its own; filed as food because its seeds are eaten.

name: Piece of tanbark
description: A curled slab of bark rich in tannin, used to tan hides.
notes: A rough 240 mm by 120 mm slab curled across, bark on top with three dark cracks, the paler inner bark showing at its edges. CHECK VOLUME is not raised; the box (x3.9) counts the curl. Tanning with it has no recipe yet.

name: Television
description: A large flat-screen television on a centre stand, full of salvageable electronics.
notes: A 42-inch set, 960 mm by 570 mm, with a charcoal bezel round a glossy black screen, a silver badge and a red standby lamp below the screen, a raised back housing and a black stand; the front faces +z. CHECK VOLUME (x6.8): the reference's 20 L ignores the air round a thin panel on a stand. Taking it apart for electronic parts has no content field yet. The size is a placeholder for a thing too big for a pack.

name: Bimetal thermostat
description: A small switch that opens and closes as a strip of two bonded metals bends with heat.
notes: 80 mm long: a steel base with two screw ears, a white ceramic block holding a brass-on-steel strip with a silver contact under a fixed contact, a brass setting screw with a black knob on a steel post, and two brass terminals with copper lugs. Using it in crafting has no recipe yet.

name: Raw tobacco leaves
description: A bunch of broad green tobacco leaves, tied at the stalks, still too fresh to smoke.
notes: Five leaf-green leaves about 250 mm long fanned from their stalks, each with a pale midrib, the stalks tied with cotton string. CHECK VOLUME (x7.9): the reference's 0.25 L is the leaves; the box counts a flat fan. Drying it into smoking tobacco needs an item state or a timed transform; the dried leaves should get their own model in plant-dried.

name: Armoured training dummy
description: A home-made wooden dummy covered in bolted scrap steel, its arms raised on guard, for practising strikes.
notes: 1.77 m tall on crossed oak feet: the light dummy's wooden post, torso, head and forward forearms, with a rusty scrap plate bolted on the chest, a galvanised belly sheet, rust-red shoulder plates and hip skirt, sheet-steel forearm tubes and shin guard, and an upturned iron bucket for a helmet with a slit. CHECK VOLUME (x9.7): the reference's 80 L is the dummy itself; the box counts the air round the feet and arms. Setting it up for melee training is a construction with no content field yet, so it has no workstation; it is crafted, so the economy entry is a placeholder. The size is a placeholder for a thing too big for a pack.

name: Training dummy
description: A home-made wooden dummy with silver tape marking where to strike.
notes: 1.77 m tall on crossed oak feet: a pine post for legs, a hip block and plank torso, a round head, shoulder blocks, upper arms hanging and forearms held forward with round fists, and silver tape crossing the chest and marking the belly, ribs, face and knee. CHECK VOLUME (x9.4): the reference's 80 L is the dummy itself; the box counts the air round the feet and arms. Setting it up for melee training is a construction with no content field yet, so it has no workstation; it is crafted, so the economy entry is a placeholder. The size is a placeholder for a thing too big for a pack.
